paragraph: Lei n.º 22/11 [was published on 17 June 2011 and entered into force that day](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2011/lei-n-o-22-11-de-17-de-junho/>). The Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD) [fined Lizíria, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, USD 115,000 in kwanzas on 10 August 2026](<https://sapo.pt/artigo/agencia-de-proteccao-de-dados-de-angola-multa-hotel-diamante-em-115-mil-dolares-6a857707bf642b2fcc16d93b>). PTI, citing the APD's register, [counted three fines totalling USD 250,000 in 2025 and five totalling USD 600,000 in 2024](<https://pti.ao/apd-ja-aplicou-mais-de-1-milhao-de-dolares-em-multas-este-ano/>). In the last twelve months, on 25 June 2026, [the Assembleia Nacional rejected a UNITA bill to amend it](<https://angop.ao/noticias/politica/parlamento-rejeita-proposta-sobre-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais/>). An APD administrator said on 17 June 2026 that [the public consultation on a new law was complete](<https://angop.ao/noticias/economia/nova-lei-de-proteccao-de-dados-pode-vigorar-no-proximo-ano-legislativo/>). No count of the APD's fines for the whole of 2026 has been found, and no date for the revised law.

Burundi's National Assembly [unanimously adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burundi-lawmakers-approve-data-protection-framework-as-digitalisation-accelerates>). The head of state [promulgated the law on 10 March 2026](<https://communityvoice.bi/1489-2/>). In the last twelve months, on 18 November 2026, the Council of Ministers [approved a draft decree on the agency's duties, membership and resources](<https://www.burunditimes.com/burundi-faces-data-protection-test-as-eac-advances-regional-rules/>), subject to adjustments. No commencement date, regulation or decision under the law has been found, and no appointment to the authority it establishes. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

Benin's data protection rules are Book V of the Code du numérique, [Law no. 2017-20, promulgated on 20 April 2018](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/loi-2017-20/download>). La Nation reported the 2025 annual report of the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles (APDP): [907 files examined, 793 validated, 64 inspection missions and 20 complaints treated](<https://www.lanation.bj/numerique/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-en-2025-au-benin-lapdp-dresse-un-bilan-sous-le-signe-de-la-conformite>). In the last twelve months, [Decree 2026-422 of 1 July 2026 appointed its eight members](<https://sgg.gouv.bj/doc/decret-2026-422/download>), who [took office on 6 November 2026](<https://www.24haubenin.info/?Les-nouveaux-membres-de-l-APDP-pretent-serment=>). On 11 November 2026 the APDP [warned content creators that publishing identifying data needs consent](<https://fraternite.bj/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-lapdp-met-en-garde-les-createurs-de-contenus/>). No source found states how many regulations are in force under the Code.

[Law n°001-2021/AN was adopted on 30 March 2021](<https://www.fonction-publique.gov.bf/fileadmin/user_upload/storage/22-08-2021-C2-LOI-N__001-2021_AN_portant_protection_des_personnes.pdf>). It makes the Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) the supervisory authority. On [26 June 2025 the CIL validated its public report for 2024](<https://cil.bf/?p=1506>). In the last twelve months, a [law adopted on 3 August 2026 merges the CSC and the CIL into a new regulator, ARCOD](<https://www.aib.media/burkina-les-deputes-adoptent-la-loi-portant-creation-de-larcod-issue-de-la-fusion-du-csc-et-de-la-cil/>). [On 19 November 2026 the Council of Ministers named the ten members of its first college](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article150924=>). No regulation under the 2021 law and no named sanction has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

Botswana's Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 18 of 2024) [came into operation on 14 January 2025](<https://itlawco.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/1736836435941.pdf>). In a public notice dated 17 July 2026 the Information and Data Protection Commission [issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM](<https://na.co.bw/data-commission-orders-suspension-of-dpsm-epayslip-portal-over-privacy-law-breaches/>). DPSM [suspended the ePayslip portal on 22 July 2026](<https://www.mmegi.bw/news/govt-e-payslip-fails-data-protection-compliance-test/news>). In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the new commissioner [vowed firmer enforcement against non-bank financial institutions](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/new-data-commission-tightens-compliance-oversight/news>). No regulation made under the Act has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled under the law, published for a period ending within the past two years.

[Loi n° 24.001 on the protection of personal data was adopted in mid-January 2024 and promulgated](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Loi_24_001_portant_protection_des_donnes_a_caractere__personnel.pdf>). It provides for a data protection agency, with the ministry in charge of the digital economy holding its missions meanwhile. [The World Bank reported in December 2024 that activities were planned to support drafting of the law's implementing decrees](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099122024184018568/txt/P1746201172f3b05d1a9d118f1eb4b91506.txt>). In the last twelve months, [on 28 January 2026 Data Protection Africa recorded the authority as not yet appointed](<https://dataprotection.africa/central-african-republic>). No regulation, decision or commencement date has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

[Decree no. 2015-79 names ARTCI](<https://www.artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/decret_2015_79.pdf>) as the body that receives declarations and imposes fines under Law no. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013. On 16 January 2024 [the authority warned the vocational training ministry and the company Kaydan Groupe](<https://www.autoritedeprotection.ci/decisions/>) and gave them formal notice. In the last twelve months, on 2 July 2026, [ARTCI launched Certinum, an online platform for compliance and authorisation requests](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2642985/economie/ntic/protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-certinum-entre-en-service-pour-accelerer-la-conformite-numerique-en-cote-divoire>). The minister said [a national register of data protection correspondents was set up in 2026](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2642003/economie/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-djibril-ouattara-presente-les-progres-realises-par-la-cote-divoire>). No yearly count of decisions has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

Cameroon's general law is [Loi n° 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on the protection of personal data](<https://prc.cm/fr/multimedia/documents/10258-loi-n-2024-017-du-23-12-2024-web>). In the last twelve months, [the law came into force on 23 June 2026](<https://www.dgb.cm/la-loi-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-entre-officiellement-en-vigueur/>), the budget directorate reported on 6 July 2026. The OBS-CC observatory reported on 12 September 2026 that [the authority had not yet been installed](<https://obs-cc.org/suivi-recommandations-fncc/>). It said the implementing decree under article 53 had not been taken. No decision, sanction or judgment applying the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

[Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023, the Digital Code, sets the rules on the protection of personal data in its Book III](<https://are.gouv.cd/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/04042023-ORDONNANCE-LOI-23-010-DU-13-MARS-PORTANT-CODE-DU-NUMERIQUE_compressed.pdf>). [A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 provisionally transferred the authority's missions to the telecommunications regulator](<https://droitnumerique.cd/arptic-arptc-investie-des-missions-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-en-rd-congo/>). In the last twelve months, on 12 March 2026, the Ministry of Digital Economy [launched a national network of data protection officers in Kinshasa](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/numerique-la-rdc-met-en-place-un-reseau-de-responsables-de-la-protection-des-donnees>). The regulator's [decision no. 039/ARPTC/CLG/2025 on prior formalities was published in the Journal officiel of 23 April 2026](<https://www.africadataprotection.org/rdc-publication-au-journal-officiel-de-la-decision-fixant-la-procedure-des-formalites-prealables.html>). No decision or sanction under the Code has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

Congo's general law is [Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/01/22/congo-launches-commission-to-strengthen-personal-data-protection-and-digital-governance/>). In the last twelve months, the [Commission's members were appointed by decree of 31 December 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/01/22/congo-launches-commission-to-strengthen-personal-data-protection-and-digital-governance/>). The same source, of 22 January 2026, reports that the National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated and elected its President, Vice President and Rapporteur. No regulation made under the law and no decision, sanction or count of complaints has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

The Union of Comoros [enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-the-comoros-data-protection-law>). The law names a Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés as the supervisory body, and [as of mid-2024 the authority had not been formally constituted](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-the-comoros-data-protection-law>). In the last twelve months, [ESCWA's profile of December 2025 said Comoros has no comprehensive data protection law in place](<https://www.unescwa.org/sites/default/files/inline-files/arab-business-legislative-frameworks-anti-corruption-comoros-english.pdf>). No source found says whether the law has commenced. No regulation or decision under it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

[Law 133/V/2001 is Cabo Verde's general data protection regime](<https://www.ibanet.org/document?id=Digital-Regulations-in-the-Metaverse-Era-Cabo-Verde>). The CNPD says it [was amended on 17 March 2021](<https://rlpd.org/cnpd-cabo-verde-um-percurso-de-onze-anos/>). The Comissão Nacional de Protecção de Dados (CNPD) report for 2023 [counts 297 processes decided out of 326 requests, and seven complaints received](<https://web.archive.org/web/20250512144516/https://tiver.cv/cnpd-apresenta-relatorio-de-atividades-de-2023/>). In the last twelve months, in April 2026, the CNPD [published an account of its eleven years](<https://rlpd.org/cnpd-cabo-verde-um-percurso-de-onze-anos/>). No change to the law has been found. No count of decisions for a year after 2023 has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

The National Assembly [passed Djibouti's first Digital Code on 30 June 2025](<https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2025/07/national-assembly-of-the-republic-of-djibouti-approves-digital-code>), with a data-protection regime embedded in it. TechHive Advisory states that the regime was [enacted in June 2025](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-djiboutis-data-protection-law>). It describes the regime as creating the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No date of promulgation or commencement, no appointment to the commission and no decision under the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

Law n° 18-07 of 10 June 2018 [came into force on 10 August 2023](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/algeria-digital-economy>), the US International Trade Administration states. The Autorité nationale de protection des données à caractère personnel (ANPDP) [adopted a deliberation on 15 July 2026](<https://anpdp.dz/ar/storage/2026/07/MOD-19-07-2026-v2.pdf>) setting conditions for processing and publishing images of people. In the last twelve months, the authority [decided in January or February 2026 that a positive or negative test result alone is standard health data](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>). No decision or sanction on a named controller has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law, Law No. 151 of 2020, [entered into force in October 2020](<https://shuralawfirm.com/en/egypt-pdpl-compliance-checklist-what-to-do-before-the-october-31-2026-deadline/>), Shura Law Firm said. The Alexandria Economic Court [ordered a telecoms operator to pay EGP 10 million in damages under the law](<https://khalfelhadth.com/41922>), as reported in 2025. In the last twelve months, in early 2026, the Personal Data Protection Center [published guidelines on consent, lawful bases, direct marketing, officers, records and breach notices](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>). [Full enforcement began in early November 2026](<https://enterpriseam.com/ai/2026/11/12/hyperscalers-want-clear-rules-before-they-build-data-centers-in-egypt/>), after a transitional period to 31 October 2026. No count of cases settled has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

Eritrea has [no comprehensive data protection law in force](<https://research.lawlab.africa/eritrea/>), as of 1 August 2026, and no supervisory authority. The Horn of Africa Initiative's update of June 2025 [placed the country at a nascent stage, without data protection legislation](<https://hoainitiative.org/sites/default/files/2025-09/25th%20HoAI%20Ministerial%20-%20Background%20Paper%20on%20Digital%20Integration%20Update.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the position [was unchanged at 1 August 2026](<https://research.lawlab.africa/eritrea/>): no law, no regulator and no enforcement. No bill or draft of a data protection law has been found. Preparing would need a data protection law announced, being drafted, before parliament, or passed and not yet promulgated.

Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 was [approved on 4 April 2024 and published in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024](<https://www.aln.africa/ethiopia-new-data-protection-law>). It names the Ethiopian Communications Authority as regulator. In November 2025 the Director General said the Authority had [received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad](<https://shega.co/news/one-year-on-ethiopia-s-personal-data-protection-law-faces-a-slow-path-to-enforcement>) and approved them as a temporary measure. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No directive under the proclamation has been found as approved, and no sanction or order on a named controller. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

[Loi n°025/2023 of 12 July 2023 amended Gabon's data protection law](<https://www.apdpvp.ga/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Gabon-Loi-025-2023-du-12-juillet-2023-portant-modification-de-la-loi-001-2011-du-25-septembre-relative-a-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel.pdf>). The authority's president said on 27 January 2026 that [its 2025 review counts 12 administrative and pecuniary sanctions](<https://www.gabonreview.com/journee-mondiale-de-la-protection-des-donnees-le-gabon-affirme-sa-strategie-face-aux-defis-du-numerique/>). In the last twelve months, on 20 January 2026, it [supervised the destruction of the personal data of unsuccessful 2022 bidders](<https://www.gabonreview.com/marches-publics-les-donnees-personnelles-des-soumissionnaires-de-2022-officiellement-detruites/>). From 10 to 20 November 2026 it [ran a campaign in Port-Gentil briefing administrations and businesses on their duties](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-port-gentil-lapdpvp-lance-une-campagne-de-sensibilisation-a-la-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-et-de-la-vie-privee/>). Whether any regulations have been issued under the law has not been found.

On 18 September 2024 a circuit court in Accra [found Bolt Holdings OU in breach of sections 20, 21, 28 and 30 of the Data Protection Act, 2012](<https://superlawgh.com/judgements/justice-noah-adade-vrs-bolt-ghana-limited/>). In the last twelve months, in January 2026, the Commission [announced that 2026 would be a year of enforcement](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/data-protection-commission-to-crack-down-on-breaches-as-2026-marked-for-strict-enforcement/>). On 14 October 2026 it [cited six named companies for operating unregistered or with expired certificates](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/10/dpc-flags-six-companies-for-data-protection-breaches/>). No regulation made under the Act has been found. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled in a year has been found. Mature would need such a count, published for a recent period.

[Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by President Alpha Condé in 2016](<https://anssi.gov.gn/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/loi_l2016037an_relative_a_la_cybersecurite_et_protection_des_do.pdf>). [In October 2025 the ministry's secretary-general said Guinea has put in place the law](<https://lepunch.net/2025/10/14/intelligence-artificielle-la-guinee-sengage-vers-une-strategie-nationale-via-un-atelier-diagnostic/>). The ministry's report on its 2025 work [says texts on personal data protection are in progress](<https://www.africaguinee.com/app/uploads/2026/01/Realisations_MPTEN_2025_compressed.pdf>), with no stage or date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation, decision or constituted authority has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

President Barrow [assented to the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act on 7 November 2025](<https://www.africanlawbusiness.com/expert-views/key-features-of-the-gambian-personal-data-protection-and-privacy-act/>). In the last twelve months, on 13 May 2026, the minister said [the country already has the law in place](<https://www.kerrfatou.com/gambia-has-ecowass-most-advanced-data-protection-law-minister-jabbi-says/>), with oversight given to the Access to Information Authority's commissioners. In November 2026 GIZ described [the Information Commission, with Commissioner Ya Amie Touray in post, as the body enforcing data protection](<https://www.giz.de/en/newsroom/stories/interview-africa-investment-climate-data-policy-builds-trust>). No commencement date has been found, and no decision, sanction or count of complaints under the Act. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

The government's February 2025 report to the Universal Periodic Review lists [a data protection bill among several awaiting discussion](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2025-09/A_HRC_WG.6_49_GNB_1_F.pdf>) in the National People's Assembly. In the last twelve months, on 8 May 2026, the Council of Ministers [approved the Data Protection Law with amendments](<https://forbesafricalusofona.com/guine-bissau-anuncia-inicio-do-recenseamento-geral-da-populacao-e-habitacao-para-junho/>). On 22 September 2026 a law professor said the country [does not yet have specific data protection legislation](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-inter-la-cour-de-justice-de-la-cedeao-dispose-dun-cadre-pour-statuer-sur-les-droits-numeriques-selon-un-universitaire/>). No source found says the bill has gone to the Assembly. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force, whether it stands alone or is part of a larger law.

[Ley Núm. 1/2016, de Protección de Datos Personales](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Guinee-equatoriale-ley-1-2.016-de-proteccion-de-datos.pdf>), was sanctioned and promulgated by the President on 22 July 2016. It names the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, to be created by a decree. It places [the power to sanction with the Minister of Telecommunications and New Technologies](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Guinee-equatoriale-ley-1-2.016-de-proteccion-de-datos.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing dated after 22 July 2016. No decree creating the Órgano Rector, regulation or decision has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was [established under the Data Protection Act, 2019](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/09/30/kenya-data-protection-commissioner-shortlist/>). An April 2025 analysis [counted 51 determinations by the office in 2024](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/11/13/kenya-data-protection-law-ai-regulation/>). In the last twelve months, in February 2026, it [ordered St Luke's Orthopaedic Hospital to compensate patients and an events company to pay KES 300,000](<https://www.amnestykenya.org/kenyas-digital-rights-journey-half-year-scorecard/>), according to Amnesty Kenya. In November 2026 [the High Court set aside a KSh1.25 million award by the office](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/11/15/odpc-compensation-powers/>). The same month [a successor to the first commissioner was nominated](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/11/10/kenya-nominates-lydia-sitienei-second-data-commissioner/>). No yearly count after 2024 has been found.

Liberia's Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024 was [approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/An_Act_For_The_Collection_Processing_-Transmission_-Storage_-Protection_-And_Use_Of_Personal-_Information_In_Liberia_Printed_Version_20260323_063904.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [President Boakai's promulgation of the law was announced on 19 August 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/gestion-publique/le-liberia-adopte-les-lois-sur-la-cybercriminalite-et-la-protection-des-donnees>). The House of Representatives had [referred the President's bill to committee on 10 June 2025](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/politics/house-reviews-privacy-data-protection-bill/article_6675211a-e8bc-43c6-8e04-e73cbf26278a.html>). No regulation, decision or sanction under the Act has been found, and no source says the Independent Information Commissioner has begun acting under it. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller.

SMEX [reported on 22 July 2026 that Libya's data protection law remains in draft](<https://smex.org/libyas-new-ai-strategy-celebrates-participation-yet-was-built-without-it/>), with adoption targeted for 2026. In January 2024 the General Information Authority reported a committee [drafting a national personal data protection law](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2024/01/24/the-committee-responsible-for-implementing-the-national-project-for-the-protection-of-personal-data-holds-its-regular-meeting-at-the-headquarters-of-the-general-information-authority/>). In the last twelve months, on 26 October 2026, the National Council and a House of Representatives committee [began a joint review of the council's draft](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=368592&lang=ar>). No source found says a government bill has been tabled. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force, whether it stands alone or is part of a larger law.

Cenfri's article of 23 March 2026 says [the Data Protection Act has been law for over a decade](<https://cenfri.org/articles/african-data-governance-reform-in-an-era-of-reform/>). It dates the Act to 2011. It also says that [the Data Protection Commission has remained unappointed](<https://cenfri.org/articles/african-data-governance-reform-in-an-era-of-reform/>), and gives no date for that position beyond its own publication. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulation made under the Act and no decision applying it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller, and a constituted supervisory authority.

The CNDP, the commission that supervises Morocco's Law 09-08 on personal data, was [installed in 2010](<https://www.cndp.ma/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/CNDP-Communiqu_2_Publication_du_Registre_National_FR_-20230111.pdf>). Moroccan courts [handled 153 personal data cases in 2024](<https://madar21.com/315419.html>), and of 109 criminal cases [80 were decided](<https://madar21.com/315419.html>). In the last twelve months the CNDP [signed a cooperation memorandum with Portugal's data protection authority on 8 February 2026](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/bimonthly-update-on-privacy-in-africa-january-february-2026>). Its president said on 4 August 2026 that a recast of the law [has been sent to the Secrétariat général du gouvernement](<https://fnh.ma/article/actualite-economique/protection-donnes-confiance-moteur-economique-numerique>). No regulation under Law 09-08 has been found, and no sanction by the CNDP on a named controller.

Madagascar's Loi n° 2014-038 on the protection of personal data was [promulgated on 9 January 2015](<https://digital.gov.mg/en/2022/07/05/loi-n-2014-038-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>). Its authority, the CMIL, [elected a president and two vice-presidents on 14 August 2025](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/11XR_I-6z6Y28qnrEjHABu3SOIbjWy6yW/view>). In the last twelve months the commission [approved its first procedures manual on 17 October 2025](<https://digital.gov.mg/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/manuel-procedures-cmil-03-dec-2025.pdf>). It also [joined the AFAPDP on 24 November 2025 and obtained a budget line of Ariary 2,411,579,000 in the 2026 Finance Law](<https://drive.google.com/file/d/11XR_I-6z6Y28qnrEjHABu3SOIbjWy6yW/view>). No decision, sanction or count of cases under the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

Mali's Law no. 2013-015 on the protection of personal data was [promulgated on 21 May 2013](<https://primature.ml/apdp-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>). For 2025 the APDP's annual report, as summarised by Sahel Tribune, counts [fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints received](<https://saheltribune.com/donnees-personnelles-lalerte-du-regulateur-malien/>). In the last twelve months the APDP [opened an extraordinary session on 6 October 2025 to review about 2,000 files](<https://fr.apanews.net/community/mali-lapdp-examine-2-000-dossiers-et-un-projet-darrete/>) and [opened a regional office at Ségou on 4 December 2025](<https://lessor.ml/posts/autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-la-region-de-segou-a-son-antenne-6932a107b56bd>). Its session of 3 August 2026 [had over 1,000 files to examine](<https://orbiteinfo.com/mali-lapdp-ouvre-sa-2e-session-2026-avec-1-000-dossiers-au-programme/>). No commencement date for the law has been found, and no figure for sanctions issued in 2026.

Mozambique has no data protection law. In April 2026 the ministry said the government had [approved the bill and sent it to the Assembly of the Republic](<https://unctad.org/system/files/non-official-document/ecn162026_s08_mr_mozambique_miquidade_en.pdf>). On 26 October 2026 the Assembly [set the plenary debate for 6 November 2026](<https://aimnews.org/2026/10/26/parlamento-alarga-calendario-de-trabalhos-para-responder-a-agenda-legislativa/>). In the last twelve months, in October 2025 the bill had [not been approved by Cabinet or sent to Parliament](<https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099012626175535228>), and on 25 August 2026 the head of INTIC said the authorities were [preparing to submit it](<https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-calls-to-strengthen-data-protection-digital-space-legislation/>). No source found says when the bill reached parliament. No data protection authority exists. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

Mauritania's Law 2017-020 on the protection of personal data was [promulgated on 22 July 2017](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/112890/MRT-112890.pdf>). Its authority, the APD, issued deliberations 004/2025 of 14 July 2025 and 005/2025 of 30 July 2025 on transfers and cloud services abroad. On 19 November 2025 the APD [approved a control reference framework and empowered its sworn agents to take part in inspection missions](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-13/>). In the last twelve months, on 29 April 2026, it [approved amendments to those two deliberations and discussed complaints 008-2025 and 001-2026](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-16/>). No sanction, order or decision on a named controller has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

Mauritius's Data Protection Act 2017 [came into force on 15 January 2018](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/Pages/The%20Law/Data-Protection-Act-2017.aspx>). For 2024 the Data Protection Office [reports 179 new complaints and 39 closed](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/AnnualReports/265-26-DPO%20AR%202024-SOFT%20COPY.pdf>), with 105 breaches notified and 112 cross-border transfers authorised. In the last twelve months, on 17 June 2026, the Minister [made regulations requiring every controller to designate a data protection officer](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/117_The-Data-Protection_Designation-Tasks-and-Position-of-Data-Protection-Officers_Reg.pdf>), from 1 January 2027. In May 2026 the Commissioner said [amendments to bring in administrative fines are being introduced](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202605/world-bank-african-dpas-outline-formula>). No figures for 2025 have been found.

Malawi's Data Protection Act, 2024 was [passed on 7 December 2023, assented to on 31 January 2024 and published on 2 February 2024](<https://www.mca.ac.mw/mca-siteup/uploads/Data%20Protection%20Act%202024.pdf>). The Authority [published a compliance guideline and checklist on 17 October 2025](<https://www.dpa.mw/download/guideline-and-checklist-on-compliance/?wpdmdl=8808>). [Breach notification guidelines followed on 22 October 2025, setting a 72-hour notice](<https://www.dpa.mw/download/guidelines-on-personal-data-breach-notifications-and-communications/?wpdmdl=8818>). In the last twelve months, on 13 July 2026, MACRA [consulted stakeholders in Blantyre on draft regulations carrying annual registration fees](<https://itweb.africa/article/malawi-advances-data-protection-framework/xnklOvz14wkq4Ymz>). No decision or sanction under the Act has been found, and no regulation in force. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

Namibia has no data protection law, and on 13 July 2026 the ICT minister, Emma Theofelus, [said that Namibia was finalising the bill](<https://itweb.africa/article/namibia-pushes-cyber-security-reforms/mQwkoq6YJWlM3r9A>). In the last twelve months the position moved. In August 2025 the minister said the bill would be [tabled in September 2025](<https://www.namibian.com.na/govt-to-introduce-data-protection-bill-in-september/>). In January 2026 she said it was [ready for resubmission to the Cabinet Committee on Legislation](<https://neweralive.na/data-legislations-under-final-polishing/>). The 2026/27 budget estimates say the committee [approved it and sent it to the justice ministry](<https://observer24.com.na/cybercrime-bill-heads-to-parliament/>). No source found says the bill has been tabled in Parliament, passed or enacted. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

Niger's [Law no. 2022-59 of 16 December 2022 on personal data protection](<https://www.hapdp.ne/uploads/files/Loi-2022-59-consolidee.pdf>) is the general law. In July 2025 the president of the HAPDP, the authority it created, said it had [processed 139 compliance files since September 2024](<https://www.lesahel.org/entretien-avec-le-president-de-la-haute-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-hapdp/>). In the last twelve months, on 13 June 2026, Africa Data Protection reported that [the government had abolished the HAPDP by decree](<https://www.africadataprotection.org/actualites/Niger-Suppression-de-la-Haute-Autorite-de-Protection-des-Donnees-a-caractere-Personnel-et-transfert-de-ses-competences.html>). The government's communiqué [confirms the decree of 8 June 2026](<https://anp.ne/niger-plusieurs-services-rattaches-ou-sous-tutelle-de-la-presidence-de-la-primature-et-du-secretariat-general-du-gouvernement-supprimes/>). No regulation made under the law and no decision under it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

President Tinubu [signed the Nigeria Data Protection Act on 12 June 2023](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/donnees-nigeria-letat-reprend-la-ndpc-apres-plus-de-9-millions-de-recettes-generees-en-3-ans/>). The Commission [fined Multichoice Nigeria N766,242,500](<https://www.rapdp.org/index.php/en/node/222>) in July 2025. A Commission order fining Meta $32.8 million was [set aside by consent judgment on 3 November 2025](<https://technext24.com/policy-and-tech/ndpc-data-protection-meta/>). In the last twelve months, on 29 July 2026, a court [ordered Stanbic IBTC Bank to pay two former customers N15 million and erase their data](<https://saharareporters.com/2026/08/01/court-slams-stanbicibtc-over-data-privacy-breach-awards-ex-customers-n15million-orders>). On 28 July 2026 the Commission [directed unregistered major controllers and processors to register](<https://punchng.com/data-commission-issues-fresh-registration-directive-following-court-victory/>). In October 2026 its chief cited [over 20 remediation orders](<https://thenigerialawyer.com/rogue-actors-are-exploiting-data-to-threaten-governance-nji-administrator-justice-adejumo-calls-for-stronger-judicial-capacity/>), giving no period. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

Rwanda's [Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>). Its [two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>). By January 2026 the National Cyber Security Authority [had registered data controllers and processors](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>). It also trained over 100 Data Protection Officers in the public sector. In the last twelve months the authority chose a theme for Data Privacy Week, 26 to 30 January 2026, and [now expects controllers to prove that they comply](<https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/32861/opinions/why-2026-is-the-year-of-accountability-for-data-controllers-and-processors>). No dated sanction or decision under the Act has been found. No source says whether regulations are issued. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

Sudan has no data protection law, and on 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers [discussed the draft data and artificial intelligence bill and directed further study](<https://sudantribune.net/article/317108>). In the last twelve months the cabinet [approved the bill on 1 November 2026](<https://www.sudanindependent.com/news/politics/2026/11/10/%D8%A5%D8%B5%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%AD-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%B2-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%B1%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%88%D8%AF%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%8A>). Its text has not been published, and no vote by the interim parliament has been found. In July 2026 an analyst wrote that [no independent body oversees data protection](<https://alakhbar-alsudan.com/?p=42822>). No regulations and no decisions have been found. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

Senegal's [Law no. 2008-12 on the protection of personal data was enacted on 25 January 2008](<https://dataprotection.africa/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Senegal-Factsheet.pdf>). For July to September 2026 the CDP [reported 214 files handled](<https://aps.sn/la-cdp-mise-sur-la-formation-et-la-sensibilisation-pour-promouvoir-la-protection-des-donnees-personnelles/>), examined 13 complaints and carried out five inspections. For April to June 2026 it [reported 195 files handled](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Societe/donnees-personnelles-plus-de-190-dossiers-traites-par-la-cdp-entre-avril-et-juin_n_503047.html>). In the last twelve months the CDP [relaunched the updating of the law at a two-day workshop at Saly, reported in July 2026](<https://lequotidien.sn/mbour-gouvernance-des-donnees-et-intelligence-artificielle-vers-un-nouveau-dispositif-normatif/>). In March 2026 [an expert said a bill was reported to be in the circuit](<https://aps.sn/donnees-personnelles-la-legislation-senegalaise-doit-etre-modernisee-et-adaptee-aux-enjeux-de-lia-expert/>). Whether any regulation is in force under the law has not been found.

Sierra Leone has no data protection law, and on 12 November 2026 the Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill [passed its second reading and was committed to the Legislative Committee](<https://sierraleoneconcordtimes.com/parliament-commits-data-protection-bill-to-legislative-committee-by-jariatu-s-bangura/>). In the last twelve months the Bill moved from [final national validation in November 2025](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/government-data-protection-information-bill>) to [Cabinet approval on 21 April 2026](<https://moice.gov.sl/cabinet-approves-first-ever-data-protection-policy-paving-way-for-new-data-law/>). In November 2026 it was [tabled in Parliament and read a first time](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/information-tables-data-protection-bills/>). No law is enacted, and no regulations or decisions have been found. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

Somalia's Law No. 005 of 2023, the Data Protection Act, [was ratified by both chambers of parliament](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/en/2024/02/26/somalia-inauguration-of-the-data-protection-authority>), and the President signed it in March 2023. The Authority was [inaugurated on 24 February 2024](<https://blog.africadataprotection.org/en/2024/02/26/somalia-inauguration-of-the-data-protection-authority>). In the last twelve months the Regulatory Framework was [approved after the Ministry of Communications and Technology said it had cleared constitutional, legal and technical procedures](<https://itweb.africa/article/somalia-adopts-data-regulatory-framework/>), reported on 6 February 2026. The Authority [opened registration of controllers and processors](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/02/somalia-data-protection-authority-enforces-nationwide-data-compliance-rules/>), reported on 2 June 2026. No named and dated decision, sanction or order under the law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

South Sudan has no data protection law, and the World Bank's identity diagnostic of 1 May 2026 says [the country has no national data protection or privacy law](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099053126171570627/pdf/P502463-0c06abde-be3d-4f83-b9e1-eca068e7bc1e.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the ICT minister [said the bill would be introduced in 2026](<https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/south-sudan-to-get-data-protection-bill-in-2026-says-minister>). A workshop of over 30 people to validate it [was reported on 5 May 2026](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/digital-rights-frontlines_dataprotection-digitalrights-cybersecurity-activity-7457423027161620480-l2o_>). On 8 September 2026 the ICT ministry's undersecretary [said the bill was still in preparation](<https://www.kictanet.or.ke/south-sudan-data-governance-workshop-juba/>). No bill tabled in parliament has been found, and no regulation or decision. Establishing would need a data protection law enacted or in force.

São Tomé and Príncipe's [Lei n.º 03/2016 on the protection of personal data was published on 10 May 2016](<https://www.dataguidance.com/sites/default/files/STP%20-%20Lei%20n.%C2%BA%2003_2016%20-%20Lei%20de%20Garantia%20e%20Protec%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20dos%20Dados%20Pessoais%20d....pdf>). In January 2026 the director of its data protection agency, the ANPDP, [said it would publish a list of non-compliant bodies and apply fines](<https://glebatv.st/todas-noticias/28-de-janeiro-sao-tome-e-principe-assinala-o-dia-internacional-da-privacidade-e-protecao-de-dados-pessoais>). In the last twelve months, on 1 June 2026, the ANPDP [signed a cooperation memorandum with Macau's data protection office](<https://www.gov.mo/pt/noticias/831008/>). No regulation made under the law has been found. No named sanction, decision or count under it has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

Eswatini's Data Protection Act, 2022 was [assented to and gazetted on 4 March 2022](<https://www.esccom.org.sz/legislation/DATA%20PROTECTION%20ACT.pdf>). The Authority lists [enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act](<https://www.edpa.org.sz/enforcement.html>), issued to MTN Eswatini and Liberty Life Swaziland Limited in June 2024 and to the Royal Science Technology Park in March 2025. In the last twelve months, in June 2026, it [opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs](<https://independentnews.co.sz/45057/news/home-affairs-investigated-for-for-sensitive-data-breach/>). In September 2026 it was [setting up information desks in major towns](<https://eswatinipositivenews.online/edpa-takes-data-protection-services-closer-to-emaswati/>). No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated year has been found. Mature would need that count published for a period ending within the past two years.

Seychelles' [Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023) was assented to on 19 December 2023 and bears the operative date 22 December 2023](<https://www.gazette.sc/sites/default/files/2023-12/Act%2024%20-%202023%20-%20Data%20Protection%20Act%202023.pdf>). The Information Commission [received four data protection cases in 2024](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Information-Commission-Annual-Report-2024.pdf>) and [14 in 2025](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/Annual-Report-2025.pdf>). In it the Chief Commissioner states that the Act remains at risk of being largely unenforced because the one budgeted technical post is unfilled. No yearly count of cases settled has been found. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

A [July 2026 analysis by the law firm Cabinet Thomas Dingamgoto](<https://thomasd-avocats.com/transfert-international-rapport-enquete-tchad-rgpd/>) applies Loi n°007/PR/2015 to personal data and treats its articles 29 to 32 as the transfer rules in force. Transfers abroad need notification to or prior authorisation from ANSICE, the National Agency for Information Security and Electronic Certification. The analysis says how far the agency acts on this is not documented. In the last twelve months the minister said on 9 December 2025 that authorities were [finalising a digital law](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1012-51293-chad-finalizes-digital-law-to-align-national-framework-with-global-standards>). On 27 April 2026 the minister [installed a committee of 34 members](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/tchad-le-gouvernement-accelere-la-refonte-du-cadre-juridique-du-numerique-pour-encadrer-lia-et-renforcer-la-souverainete-digitale/>) to propose modernised digital texts. No regulation, decision or sanction under the 2015 law has been found. Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

Togo's [Loi n° 2019-014 of 29 October 2019](<https://jo.gouv.tg/sites/default/files/JO/JOS_29_10_2019-64E%20ANNEE-N%C2%B026%20TER.pdf>) on the protection of personal data was adopted and promulgated. Its authority, the Instance de protection des données à caractère personnel (IPDCP), [officially launched its activities in Lomé on 28 March 2025](<https://www.togofirst.com/fr/tic/2903-16040-numerique-l-instance-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-demarre-ses-activites>). In the last twelve months it [signed a cooperation memorandum with the broadcast regulator HAAC on 10 December 2025](<https://cybersecuritymag.africa/la-haac-et-ipdcp-scellent-un-accord-de-cooperation-institutionnelle>). On 18 November 2026 it [certified its first 28 correspondents](<https://ipdcp.tg/protection-des-donnees-personnelles-28-correspondants-certifies-par-lipdcp/>) for three years. Tunisia's [organic law 2004-63 of 27 July 2004](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/loi-organique-n-2004-63-du-27-juillet-2004-portant-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>) sets the rules for processing, consent and rights, and was still in force in September 2026. In February 2026 a health ministry official [told the Assembly that its authority, the INPDP, has ceased its activities since 2024](<https://www.webdo.tn/fr/actualite/national/protection-des-donnees-audition-strategique-a-larp-sur-la-future-loi-organique/393696/>). Operating would need a dated sanction, order, decision or court judgment on a controller within the past three years.

Tanzania's [Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 11 of 2022, Chapter 44) commenced on 1 May 2023](<https://www.pdpc.go.tz/media/media/THE_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_ACT.pdf>). On 19 August 2025 the Commission [ruled in Complaint No. PDPC/CMP/002/2025 against the operator of an Instagram business page](<https://fbattorneys.co.tz/instagram-photo-triggers-payment-of-fine/>), awarding damages of TZS 20 million and a fine of TZS 5 million. In the last twelve months, on 8 January 2026, the Minister [gave unregistered institutions a final three months to register](<https://www.pdpc.go.tz/core/en/minister-kairuki-issues-final-three-month-ultimatum-on-personal-data-registration2026-02-02-133701/>). Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.

Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, is in force, and the statistics bureau [dates it to 2019](<https://unstats.un.org/unsd/demographic-social/meetings/2025/genderstat-forum-10/docs/Session8.2-Uganda-Johnstone-updated.pdf>). On 18 July 2025 the Personal Data Protection Office [found Google LLC in breach and ordered it to register within 30 days](<https://pdpo.go.ug/media/2025/07/Ssekamwa-Frank-3-Ors-vs-Google-LLC-PDPO-Decision-18th-July-2024.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 3 December 2025 a magistrate [fined the finance manager of Vuka Africa Ltd sh100,000 for failing to register](<https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/news/kampala-data-collection-company-prosecuted-ov-NV_224311_032026>). No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated period has been found. Mature would need such a count published for a period ending within the past two years.

South Africa's [Protection of Personal Information Act of 2013](<https://www.businessday.co.za/news/law/2026-08-17-information-regulator-goes-to-the-sca-in-new-bid-to-stop-publication-of-matric-results/>) has been [in force since 1 July 2021](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/popia-grace-period-limits-regulators-fines/P3gQ2qGAlAk7nRD1>). In 2024/25 the Information Regulator [received 1,355 complaints under it and resolved 745](<https://inforegulator.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Information-Regulator-Annual-Report-2025-210mm-x-260mm-1.pdf>). Zimbabwe's Cyber and Data Protection Act, No. 5 of 2021, was [gazetted on 11 March 2022](<https://www.veritaszim.net/sites/veritas_d/files/Cyber%20%26%20Data%20Protection%20Act%20Cap1207%20No%205%20of%202021%20gaz%202022-03-11.pdf>). By October 2025 POTRAZ had [received 20 formal complaints and investigated and resolved 15](<https://privacyscorecardreport.com/privacy-scorecard-report-2025/zimbabwe/zimbabwes-data-protection-regime/>). By November 2026 it had [issued over 195 enforcement notices and licensed over 2,500 controllers](<https://postonsunday.co.zw/2026/11/12/potraz-puts-zimbabwe-on-africas-digital-map/>). In the last twelve months, [Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026, published in July 2026, announced mandatory compliance inspections of data controllers from 1 September 2026](<https://www.techzim.co.zw/2026/07/potraz-starts-data-protection-inspections-on-1-september-here-is-what-it-means-for-you/>). No count of decisions for a stated year has been found, and no named sanction. Mature would need a count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled, published for a period ending within the past two years.
